IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
RASHMI KANT VIJAY CHANDRA & ORS. v. BAIJNATH CHOUBEY & COMPANY
Citation: 2024 INSC 688 | Civil Appeal No. 10452 of 2024
Bench: Supreme Court of India
Date of Judgment: September 13, 2024
JUDGMENT & LEGAL PRINCIPLES
This civil appeal arises from an eviction suit governed by tenancy laws and concerns the scope of High Court
jurisdiction under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) when dealing with second appeals
against concurrent or factual findings of First Appellate Courts.
FACTUAL & PROCEDURAL HISTORY
The plaintiffs (appellants) instituted an eviction suit against the defendant-firm alleging illegal sub-letting without
consent. The First Appellate Court decreed the suit in favor of the landlords after examining evidence of
sub-tenancy. However, the High Court of Calcutta reversed the decree in second appeal without explicitly
framing a substantial question of law.
RATIO DECIDENDI & COURT FINDINGS
1. Section 100 CPC Mandate: The Supreme Court held that the High Court committed a manifest error of law
by disturbing factual findings of the First Appellate Court without formulating and deciding a substantial question
of law as statutorily required under Section 100 CPC.
2. Estoppel & Procedural Objections: The Court observed that a defendant-partner who appears and
participates in proceedings following notice cannot subsequently challenge non-joinder of other partners if such
objection was not raised in the initial written statement.
3. Ground of Sub-letting: The Court upheld the First Appellate Court's finding that unauthorized creation of
sub-tenancy entitled the landlord to an eviction decree under applicable premises tenancy legislation.
ORDER & DISPOSITION
The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court's judgment, and restored the decree of
eviction in favor of the plaintiff-appellants.
